executive_summary: The supplied evidence shows that the current 1h direction CatBoost topology model is not yet feature-led: calendar and symbol features dominate, topology-only underperforms calendar-only on the held-out test split, and the combined ablation stops at iteration 1 with most topology features at zero importance. In contrast, contrarian-sweep and strong-contrarian targets show materially stronger classification lift, especially in top-fraction ranking, but the economic backtests shown for squeeze configurations are negative or approximately breakeven after 14 bps round-trip costs. The main audit priority is not hyperparameter search; it is target/feature/execution alignment: add measurable temporal liquidity-state features, volatility/distance normalization, calibration diagnostics, regime and multi-timeframe alignment tests, redundancy controls, and oracle-safe execution simulation before expanding model tuning.

findings.title: The 1h direction model is dominated by symbol/calendar effects, not topology structure

evidence.detail: calendar_only test balanced_accuracy is 0.4501181944262669; topology_only test balanced_accuracy is 0.4038438389491346; combined test balanced_accuracy is 0.44096298934188555, which is -0.009155205084381335 versus calendar.

Combined feature importance is concentrated in symbol, dow_sin, is_weekend_utc, hour_sin, hour_cos, log1p_lower_total_volume, log1p_upper_total_volume and dow_cos; most topology distance/imbalance features have 0.0 importance.

findings.why_it_matters: If topology features do not add out-of-sample lift beyond calendar and symbol, the model may be learning asset/session priors rather than actionable liquidity topology.
findings.verification_test: Run a walk-forward ablation with identical folds for: calendar_only, symbol_only, topology_static_only, topology_dynamic_only, topology_plus_calendar, and full. Include permutation importance by fold and group results by symbol/timeframe.
findings.recommended_change: Do not start broad hyperparameter search yet. First redesign topology features and require topology-added lift over calendar/symbol baselines under walk-forward validation.
findings.success_metric: Across at least 3 chronological folds, topology_plus_calendar improves test balanced_accuracy or ROC/PR metric by at least 0.02 absolute versus calendar_plus_symbol, and at least 70% of folds show non-negative topology-added lift.
findings.risk: Calendar effects can be regime-specific and may decay; deploying a calendar-dominated liquidity model risks poor generalization.

findings.title: Combined 1h direction ablation stops at iteration 1 and suppresses most topology features

evidence.detail: combined best_iteration is 1, validation log_loss is 1.090541819034665 and test log_loss is 1.0891496553612698.

Features including nearest_side, has_lower_level, has_topology, nearest_side_code, upper_distance_pct, lower_distance_pct, distance_advantage, signed_distance_edge, active_level_difference, active_level_total, topology_imbalance and many volume-ratio fields have 0.0 importance.

findings.why_it_matters: A model stopping after one boosting iteration is usually not a reliable representation of feature value. It can hide useful interactions or indicate loss/validation mismatch, excessive regularization, noisy target, class weighting instability, or a weak split design.
findings.verification_test: Repeat the combined ablation with fixed CatBoost parameters but multiple eval metrics: MultiClass log_loss, TotalF1 macro, balanced accuracy evaluated externally, and no early stopping for a diagnostic run. Compare learning curves and feature importances across folds.
findings.recommended_change: Before tuning depth/learning rate, audit early stopping and objective/metric alignment. Use external fold metrics for model selection instead of relying only on a single validation best_iteration.
findings.success_metric: Learning curves should show stable validation improvement beyond trivial iteration counts, and non-calendar feature importances should be stable across folds with rank correlation greater than 0.5 for the top 15 features.
findings.risk: Current feature conclusions may be false negatives if early stopping selected an underfit model.

findings.title: Core topology CatBoost feature sets are mostly static snapshots and lack explicit liquidity velocity, persistence, replenishment and post-sweep-state features

evidence.detail: Baseline features include distances, volume aggregates, active level counts, ratios and calendar fields, but no explicit age, velocity, persistence, replenishment, prior-sweep or post-sweep-state columns are listed.

MODEL_FEATURES include current_price, upper/lower distances, pool/total volumes, active levels, ratios and calendar features, but no explicit temporal cluster velocity, liquidity age, replenishment after hit, or persistence duration features are listed.

A separate forecast_v1 dataset builder creates lagged deltas/change ratios and multi-timeframe features, showing temporal feature engineering exists elsewhere, but these are not evidenced in the baseline 1h CatBoost feature lists.

findings.why_it_matters: Market microstructure topology is path-dependent. Static nearest-level distance and volume can miss whether a liquidity cluster is building, decaying, replenishing after sweeps, or repeatedly rejected.
findings.verification_test: Add features per symbol/timeframe using only prior snapshots: level_age_minutes, nearest_side_stability_minutes, distance_velocity over 5/15/30/60m, pool_volume_velocity, active_level_velocity, replenishment_ratio_after_sweep, prior_sweep_count_1h/4h, post_sweep_elapsed_minutes, and cluster_persistence_score. Run feature ablations against the current static set.
findings.recommended_change: Promote temporal topology features from research datasets into the main CatBoost training pipeline, with strict backward-only computation and embargo-aware validation.
findings.success_metric: Dynamic topology feature block improves target-specific validation: for direction_1h, at least +0.02 balanced_accuracy over static topology; for strong_contrarian_25bp, at least +0.02 PR-AUC or +10% relative top_5pct lift over the current full_combined model.
findings.risk: Poorly implemented temporal features can leak future state if not computed with groupwise backward windows only.

findings.title: The observed core features use raw percent distances and log volumes but no explicit volatility-normalized distance or liquidity-normalized volume

evidence.detail: Numeric features include upper_distance_pct, lower_distance_pct, distance_advantage, signed_distance_edge, log1p distance features and log1p volume features, but no ATR, realized volatility, spread, or rolling volume normalization fields are listed.

Feature generation creates log1p transforms, active level counts, volume imbalance, signed_distance_edge and calendar encodings. It does not show ATR, realized volatility, rolling dollar-volume normalization, or distance-in-volatility-units.

findings.why_it_matters: A 25 bps level has different meaning in low-volatility versus high-volatility regimes. Raw pool volume also has different meaning by symbol and session.
findings.verification_test: Create backward-only normalized features: upper_distance_to_realized_vol_15m/60m, lower_distance_to_realized_vol, distance_to_ATR, pool_volume_to_rolling_symbol_median, total_volume_zscore_by_symbol_timeframe, and liquidity_pressure_per_volatility. Compare against raw/log-only features.
findings.recommended_change: Normalize distances and liquidity by recent realized volatility and symbol/timeframe-specific rolling liquidity baselines before additional CatBoost tuning.
findings.success_metric: Normalized feature block should reduce symbol importance dependence and improve out-of-sample ranking: at least +0.01 ROC-AUC or +0.02 PR-AUC on contrarian targets, or at least +0.02 balanced_accuracy on direction/sweep classification.
findings.risk: Rolling normalizers can introduce lookahead if windows are centered or fit using validation/test rows.

findings.title: Feature lists contain many raw/log duplicate and algebraically related features

evidence.detail: LOG1P_COLUMNS include current_price, distances, distance_advantage, pool volumes, ratios, active levels and total volumes, creating both raw and log1p variants.

Both distance_advantage and log1p_distance_advantage are highly important; both pool_volume_ratio and log1p_pool_volume_ratio appear; both distance_pressure_ratio and log1p_distance_pressure_ratio appear.
Raw and log variants coexist for distances, total volumes, active levels, pool volumes and ratios.

findings.why_it_matters: CatBoost can handle correlated features, but excessive redundant variants can make importances unstable, increase search space, and hide which economic quantity matters.
findings.verification_test: Run foldwise feature clustering by Spearman correlation and SHAP/permutation importance. Compare full features against a de-duplicated set that keeps either raw, log, z-scored, or normalized versions per feature family.
findings.recommended_change: Use a feature-family registry: choose canonical raw/log/normalized variants per block, then allow CatBoost interactions rather than feeding all related transforms blindly.
findings.success_metric: A reduced feature set within 70% of current feature count should preserve at least 99% of validation ROC-AUC/PR-AUC or balanced_accuracy while improving fold-to-fold importance stability.
findings.risk: Over-pruning can remove useful nonlinear threshold information; changes must be validated by ablation rather than by correlation alone.

findings.title: Global models rely heavily on symbol categorical features; per-symbol versus global performance is not fully resolved in supplied model reports

evidence.detail: symbol importance is 28.734358107927594 in topology_only.
Group metrics vary by symbol and fold. For example, fold_3 base_rate ranges from 0.01439292690449265 for XAUUSDT to 0.07380033396293559 for ETHUSDT, and ROC-AUC varies by symbol.
A diagnostics script exists for group performance by symbol, timeframe and symbol_timeframe, but the corresponding output CSV files are not supplied.

findings.why_it_matters: A single global model can learn symbol priors instead of invariant topology behavior. Conversely, per-symbol models can overfit if sample sizes are small. The supplied evidence does not settle this tradeoff.
findings.verification_test: Train and evaluate: global_with_symbol, global_without_symbol, per_symbol, per_symbol_timeframe, and hierarchical/global-plus-symbol-calibrated variants using identical walk-forward folds.
findings.recommended_change: Keep a global model only if it beats per-symbol and no-symbol baselines on both average and worst-group metrics. Otherwise use symbol-specific calibration or specialist heads.
findings.success_metric: Selected architecture should improve macro average group metric while not reducing worst-symbol ROC-AUC/PR-AUC or balanced_accuracy by more than 0.01 versus the best specialist baseline.
findings.risk: Removing symbol too early may degrade real signal; keeping it without controls may overstate generalization.

findings.title: Backtests use CatBoost probabilities for thresholding, but calibration evidence is missing

evidence.detail: Alerts are selected from validation full-stream squeeze_probability percentiles and filtered by direction_confidence.
Signals are generated using absolute squeeze_probability thresholds and direction_confidence thresholds.
Log_loss is reported for validation and test, but no Brier score, expected calibration error, reliability curve, or probability calibration method is reported.

findings.why_it_matters: Percentile and confidence thresholds depend on ranking and calibration stability. Uncalibrated probabilities can shift across folds, symbols and regimes, causing unstable alert rates.
findings.verification_test: For each fold and symbol, compute reliability curves, ECE/MCE, Brier score, probability quantile stability and threshold transfer from validation to test. Compare raw CatBoost probabilities with temperature scaling, isotonic calibration and Platt calibration fitted on validation only.
findings.recommended_change: Add a calibration layer and report calibrated versus raw performance before selecting alert thresholds.
findings.success_metric: Calibration should reduce ECE by at least 30% without reducing ROC-AUC/PR-AUC by more than 0.005, and validation-selected alert percentiles should produce test alert counts within ±25% of expected counts per fold.
findings.risk: Over-calibration on small validation windows can reduce ranking quality; calibration methods must be fold-local and time-safe.

findings.title: Execution-aligned contrarian targets show stronger predictive structure than generic 1h direction labels

evidence.detail: Generic direction_1h CatBoost test balanced_accuracy is 0.45233489465979143 and test macro_f1 is 0.4517995120639236.
full_combined contrarian-sweep test ROC-AUC is 0.6334127393936885 and balanced_accuracy is 0.5961466080942465.
full_combined strong_contrarian_25bp test ROC-AUC is 0.7187444457133587, PR-AUC is 0.1280341788404858, and top_5pct lift is 3.020426899242598.
Walk-forward test ROC-AUC values are 0.6917950579855128, 0.6973569034001634 and 0.7196391207030284 across folds.

findings.why_it_matters: The topology problem appears better framed as event/sweep/continuation ranking than generic future direction classification. Loss and target structure should match the intended trade trigger and payoff asymmetry.
findings.verification_test: Compare targets under identical folds and feature sets: direction_1h, sweep_first_side_1h, farther_side_swept_first, strong_contrarian_10bp, strong_contrarian_25bp, and direct execution-outcome labels. Evaluate ranking, calibration and economic simulation separately.
findings.recommended_change: Prioritize execution-aligned binary/ranking objectives for sweep and continuation probability. Treat generic direction_1h as a diagnostic baseline, not the primary model objective.
findings.success_metric: Chosen target should maintain walk-forward test ROC-AUC above 0.68 or PR-AUC lift above 2x base rate in top 5% across all folds, and then pass an oracle-safe economic simulation after costs.
findings.risk: Better classification lift does not imply profitable execution; do not infer financial performance from AUC or lift alone.

findings.title: Supplied squeeze backtests do not demonstrate robust positive net expectancy after costs

evidence.detail: Best configuration has 72 trades, mean_net_bps -3.3333093933307953, median_net_bps -15.004219142807239, profit_factor 0.79241506507768 and minimum_fold_mean_bps -10.956375532745634 with 14 bps round-trip cost.

Best-by-research-score configuration has 68 trades, mean_net_bps -0.0495200280758433 and profit_factor 0.9955974240039208; another top-20 configuration has mean_net_bps 2.3990438150017255 but only 1 positive fold out of 3 and minimum_fold_mean_bps -16.50064724682092.

findings.why_it_matters: Event precision and direction accuracy can be high while the execution rule still loses after costs because stops, adverse excursion, latency and target placement dominate.
findings.verification_test: Decompose each alert into pre-event lead, entry slippage, MFE/MAE before entry, stop/target distance distribution, and outcome by event_detected/event_direction_correct. Run paired comparison of no-trade, fixed target/stop, nearest-liquidity target/stop and volatility-scaled exits.
findings.recommended_change: Separate signal-quality optimization from execution optimization. Require net-after-cost validation before ranking configurations by research score.
findings.success_metric: For any candidate execution rule, require positive mean_net_bps in all walk-forward folds, minimum_fold_profit_factor above 1.0, and enough trades to estimate uncertainty; otherwise classify as research-only.
findings.risk: Small trade counts and broad grid search can overfit apparent positives; no financial performance should be promised.

findings.title: Many grid configurations produce identical top metrics, suggesting inactive or non-binding hyperparameters

evidence.detail: Top configurations 3934 through 5394 have identical metrics across minimum_direction_confidence values 0.55 to 0.70 and minimum_target_distance_bps 0, 25 and 50.
Top configurations 2278, 2279, 2764, 2765, 3250, 3251, 3736 and 3737 have identical metrics despite different minimum_direction_confidence and minimum_target_distance_bps settings.

findings.why_it_matters: If grid dimensions are non-binding, the search overstates exploration and can hide which variables actually control behavior.
findings.verification_test: For each grid parameter, compute unique alert sets, unique trade sets, and metric deltas. Flag parameters where changing the parameter changes zero alerts or zero trades across most configurations.
findings.recommended_change: Prune inactive grid dimensions or widen parameter ranges only after confirming the implementation path is correct. Report parameter sensitivity, not just top configurations.
findings.success_metric: Every retained grid dimension should change alert count, trade count, or risk/return metrics in at least 20% of configurations, unless explicitly documented as a guardrail.
findings.risk: Continuing broad searches over inactive knobs increases multiple-testing risk without improving model understanding.

findings.title: Strong-contrarian economic backtest uses precomputed sweep label columns to determine whether and when a trade triggers

evidence.detail: The backtest loads SWEEP_LABEL_PATH columns sweep_code_1h and first_hit_seconds_1h and passes them into simulate_candidate.
simulate_candidate returns None unless sweep_code_1h equals the required farther-side sweep code, and uses first_hit_seconds_1h to compute expected_hit_time_ns and entry_index.
sweep_code_1h and first_hit_seconds_1h are built by inspecting later prices inside the future horizon.

findings.why_it_matters: Even if this is intended to emulate a resting stop order that triggers only when the far level is swept, using future label columns in the simulator is a high-risk design. A bug or mismatch can convert future knowledge into execution filtering.
findings.verification_test: Reimplement the same backtest without sweep label columns: at signal time, place a conditional trigger at the far liquidity level, scan the subsequent observed price stream online, enter only when price crosses the trigger, cancel on near-side invalidation if applicable, and compare trade IDs, entry times and returns against the label-driven version.
findings.recommended_change: Remove sweep_code_1h and first_hit_seconds_1h from economic backtest decision paths. Use only price stream, known levels at signal time, and online trigger logic.
findings.success_metric: Oracle-free online simulation should match label-driven trigger timing within one snapshot for at least 99% of trades, or differences must be explained and the label-driven report retired.
findings.risk: If not corrected, economic results for this strategy may be materially optimistic or invalid.

findings.title: Regime and multi-timeframe matrix/topology alignment research exists, but integration into the audited core CatBoost models is not evidenced

evidence.detail: Matrix features are computed for 1h, 4h and 24h, merged into forecast_v3/matrix_topology_dataset.parquet, and include matrix_mtf_direction, matrix_mtf_agreement_strength and matrix_topology_direction_agreement.
The script builds cohorts such as MATRIX_FULL_ALIGNMENT, MATRIX_24H_4H_ALIGNMENT, TOPOLOGY_MATRIX_AGREEMENT and TOPOLOGY_MATRIX_CONFLICT.
The CatBoost 1h feature list does not include matrix_* or multi-timeframe alignment columns.

findings.why_it_matters: Liquidity clusters behave differently under aligned trend regimes, mixed regimes and topology/matrix conflict. Without explicit regime conditioning, a global model can average incompatible behaviors.
findings.verification_test: Add matrix/topology alignment features to the same walk-forward CatBoost pipeline and run interaction ablations: topology only, matrix only, topology plus matrix, and topology-by-regime specialist models.
findings.recommended_change: Integrate regime features only after proving no lookahead in matrix_available_at ASOF joins. Evaluate models by regime cohort and symbol.
findings.success_metric: Regime-aware model improves top-fraction lift or PR-AUC by at least 10% relative on strong_contrarian_25bp, or improves worst-regime metric without reducing overall metric by more than 0.005.
findings.risk: Matrix features built from OHLCV candles must be available only after candle close; incorrect alignment could leak future candle information.

missing_evidence: CatBoost hyperparameter search logs and exact training scripts for data/models/topology_v2_catboost_1h are not supplied.
Calibration reports such as ECE, Brier score, reliability curves and calibrated probability comparisons are not supplied.
The economic backtest report for data/backtests/topology_v2_strong_contrarian_25bp is not supplied; only the script is supplied.
Outputs from scripts/diagnose_topology_v2_baseline_1h.py group, probability and confidence reports are not supplied.
Feature schema for data/features/liq_topology_v2.parquet before build_topology_v2_ml_features.py is only partially inferable from required columns.
No explicit latency, spread, order book depth, market order flow, or funding/open-interest features are evidenced.
No SHAP values, permutation importances, foldwise feature stability reports, or feature correlation reports are supplied.
No per-symbol versus global model comparison report is supplied.
No production inference contract proving feature availability times for every feature is supplied.
No statistical confidence intervals or bootstrapped uncertainty estimates for backtest means are supplied.
top_3_next_actions: Replace label-driven strong-contrarian execution simulation with oracle-free online trigger simulation using only known levels and future observed prices, then compare trade-level outputs.
Build a walk-forward feature-ablation suite that separates calendar/symbol, static topology, dynamic topology, volatility-normalized topology, matrix/regime, and combined feature blocks.
Add probability calibration and threshold-transfer diagnostics before further grid or hyperparameter search.
